subject: FinLytics implementation: model choices, context scenarios & peak token estimates
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Handoff: FinLytics model shortlist + context/token scenarios

Hi Olga / Grace —

Looping you in to hand off FinLytics for implementation. Quick summary up front and attachments with the raw profiling: finlytics_model_shortlist_v1.pdf (recommended models and perf), finlytics_token_profile.csv (sampleed prompt/response distributions).

What we learned during discovery and the asks from the product team at FinLytics (Alex):
- Use case: real-time account summarization and regulatory note generation inside their analyst UI.
- Input prompt mix: long context (user uploads + 3-5 prior messages) + short live queries. Typical input token length sampled ~400–800 tokens; 95th percentile hits ~3,200 tokens.
- Desired outputs: concise summaries (~150–400 tokens) and occasional long-form regulatory notes (~1,200 tokens).
- Peak traffic expectation (customer provided): 40–50 requests/sec during market open spikes; steady state ~6–10 rps.
- SLO: interactive feel, median response <600ms for short summaries; can accept 2–3s for long notes.

Model shortlist & initial recommendation (see PDF for latency/cost estimates):
1) Redwood-13B-chat (8-bit) — balanced cost/latency for short summaries; good for A/B baseline.
2) Mistral-30B-instruct (ptq) — stronger long-form quality, higher cost; useful for regulatory notes.
3) Llama-70B-ptq (reduced precision) — best at longer context quality, use as fallback for worst-case quality needs.

Context window guidance:
- For summaries: limit prefix to last ~3,000 tokens (truncate older uploads) to meet latency target.
- For notes: allow up to 8k context when generating long-form; run these on dedicated capacity or scheduled longer tail batch to avoid impacting latency SLOs.

Token volume estimate (monthly projection based on FinLytics forecast):
- Baseline month: 12M requests -> ~5B input tokens, ~1.8B output tokens
- Peak month (market events): up to 3x baseline token volume

Action items for implementation team (initial):
- Olga: run two quick load profiles with Redwood-13B-chat and Mistral-30B using the sample token profile (attached). Report p95 latency at 4k and 8k context.
- Set up prefix/KV caching for frequently requested account histories.
- Define canary: 5% traffic for Mistral-30B (long-form) and 25% for Redwood-13B for summary route.

Let me know if you need anything else. Alex is on CC and can confirm the traffic numbers / procurement timeline if needed.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Mercer <alex@finlytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: FinLytics model shortlist + context/token scenarios

Thanks Monica — taking this on. A few clarifying questions before I run the profiles:

1) Prompt mix detail: is the ~3,200 token 95th percentile for the combined prompt+attachments? And for the long-form regulatory notes, does the 1,200-token output assume the full 8k context is provided or a condensed prompt?
2) Do they plan to call embeddings for retrieval at request time, or will retrieval be pre-indexed and we only send retrieved chunks? That affects batching and token counts.
3) Latency windows: you note <600ms median for short summaries — do we have an explicit p95 target? That will guide whether we prioritize smaller-model low-latency configs vs larger models.

I'll start with two test configs this afternoon:
- Config A: Redwood-13B-chat, 4k context cap, 8 concurrent streams, dynamic batching enabled
- Config B: Mistral-30B-ptq, 8k context, reserved instance for canary traffic only

I'll attach the raw perf outputs and a short ops runbook. Expected ETA for first perf run: tomorrow EOD Pacific.

From: Alex Mercer <alex@finlytics.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: FinLytics model shortlist + context/token scenarios

Hi Olga — thanks for taking this on. Quick clarifications to help with the profile:

- The 3,200 token 95th percentile is for the combined prompt + the most recent uploaded document chunk we include in the prompt; our retrieval returns ~2–5 chunks prefiltered, so that number already accounts for typical retrieval.
- The 1,200-token note output assumes we provide a 6–8k context window for the generator; we can also accept a two-phase flow (short summary + background expansion) if that's operationally cheaper.
- Embeddings: we run retrieval offline and pass top-K chunks (not calling embedding at request time).
- Expected daily traffic: 4.5M requests/day on peak days (market open bursts) — we expect sustained spikes lasting 2–3 hours. Peak concurrency estimate ~45 qps.
- PII: some documents contain masked account numbers and redacted names; full PII is not expected to flow into prompts. We will provide a redaction checklist for compliance.

Procurement timeline: procurement@finlytics.com is working on PO and expects to finalize next week. I'll attach the procurement packet in a separate message.

—Alex
Product Lead | FinLytics
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Mercer <alex@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: FinLytics model shortlist + context/token scenarios — implementation plan

Thanks everyone — confirmation and next steps from CS/implementation side:

1) Olga: proceed with the two perf runs Monica listed. Prioritize collecting p50/p95 latency and token burn per request across the 4k and 8k cap points. Please include cold-start and warm-cache runs.
2) Ops: request a small Dedicated pool for the Mistral-30B canary (estimated 2x A100-equivalent for 5% traffic). We will revisit sizing after perf numbers.
3) Canary plan: start 5% traffic for long-form route -> 25% for summary route on Redwood-13B for one week, measure quality delta (prompt-set A/B) and cost. If quality lifts > 8% (customer-defined metric in the PDF), expand.
4) Security/compliance: Monica, please collect the redaction checklist and send SOC2 evidence links to Alex. Procurement packet will be attached to this thread by Alex; once received we'll open a billing ticket.
5) Timeline: perf runs by Olga (tomorrow EOD), canary ready by next Tue (7/27) if procurement clears.

I'll own stakeholder comms and the rollout checklist. Olga — ping me if you hit any infra blockers and I'll escalate.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
